A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and relocation into v2's electronic companion.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix B report original Llama-2 experiments on 50 synthetic queries, including advertiser rewards, payments, utilities, and regression analyses.

after.justification: Section 6 and EC.3 retain those original experiments and add a comparison of participation utility with and without the payment offset.

M1.justification: V1 Algorithm 2 becomes v2 Algorithm 1, with the context-aware model renamed from pi_gen to pi_con. The reference-only baseline remains a special case. Candidate generation, softmax reweighting, payment construction, and utility offset are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic advertising task using 50 queries with two fictitious advertisers each. The musical-instrument example is retained, including its fuller presentation in v2 Table EC.1. No additional dataset or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: V2 Figure EC.1 adds without-offset counterparts to the utility-versus-candidate-count comparison; v1 Figure 2b reports utility curves only with the offset. Without-offset variants already participated in v1's correlation and scatter analyses, so this is a limited extension of comparator participation.

E3.justification: The Llama-2-7b-chat-hf model, temperature 0.8, top-p 0.95, regularization parameter 1, and candidate-count sweep remain unchanged. Renaming reward and utility 'gains' as 'normalized' quantities preserves their definitions. The added offset plots use the existing experimental setup.

E4.justification: Figure EC.1 adds an analysis of how the payment offset affects expected participation utility across candidate counts, separately for reference and context-aware generation. Existing reward–utility correlation and scatter analyses remain available; removing a duplicate main-text scatter panel does not remove that analysis.

E5.justification: The 25 seeds per query, 1,250 instances, and 95% confidence-interval reporting remain unchanged. However, v2 omits v1's disclosure that scatter/regression analyses use more than four candidates and exclude the top and bottom 0.5 percentiles of both metrics. This loses estimation detail without establishing that fits or runs changed.

E6.justification: Figure EC.1 newly reports without-offset utility trajectories alongside the retained offset results. Existing main findings and scatter-fit values remain unchanged: context-aware R-squared/slope pairs are 0.61/0.52 and 0.12/0.40; reference-model pairs are 0.96/1.00 and 0.19/0.50. No same-setting performance improvement is established.

T1.justification: V2 explicitly states the proposal-distribution support requirement for convergence in Section 4. Conversely, v1's proof of Lemma 5.5, including Equation (16), is omitted although its utility identity survives as Lemma 1. Most other proofs are relocated to EC.1–EC.2 rather than changed.

C1.justification: The central claims remain convergence to the regularized optimum without fine-tuning, truthful bidding before convergence, contextual acceleration, and equitable participation benefits. Advertising becomes more prominent in the abstract, but the broader applicability to preference aggregation with monetary transfers is retained.

C2.justification: EC.3.4 explicitly explains that the offset raises utility for both variants but does not make reference-only participation beneficial. Positive utility for the context-aware variant is qualified by advertisers being relevant to the query. V1 emphasizes reward–utility alignment without this explicit interpretation of the offset's participation limits.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 clarifies inference costs and corrects the stated call count under linear reward approximation from n to M LLM calls. Scatter-data filtering instructions disappear. Prompts, hardware, hyperparameters, and the promise of future code and data release are retained in EC.3.

R1.justification: V2 adds Bommasani et al. and Peters and Schaal, crediting the latter for the optimal-distribution solution previously attributed to Rafailov et al. It removes Parkes and Seuken. The substantive positioning against Duetting, Dubey, and the other related mechanisms remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and much of the main narrative are extensively rewritten and condensed. Algorithm exposition is consolidated, practical remarks become Section 4.1, and proofs and detailed settings move into EC.1–EC.3. Terminology shifts toward 'strategyproof'; the author block also changes while running headers retain the earlier names.

P2.justification: V2 adopts different typography, running headers, and extensive display redistribution. Figures 1b and 2 receive corrected reward, revenue, and utility axes; Figure 3 loses its duplicate scatter panel and changes its vertical range. Table 1 is shortened with a fuller companion copy, and Figure EC.1 is added.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the contribution easier to assess through streamlined exposition, corrected plot labels, and a direct offset-utility analysis that clarifies participation benefits and limits. These are useful but limited gains because the method and principal results remain stable. The omitted equity-lemma derivation and regression-filtering disclosure partially offset the improvement.
